brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 — in exchange for a price cut of about 12%, freeing up ₹26.60 L in cash for us and giving them cash 15 days earlier when they need it (their cash is stuck for 101 days, far longer than competitors at 64).

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut of roughly 12% in exchange for paying them 15 days faster.
priceAsk.target: A saving of around 12% on our ₹6.47 Cr annual spend — their borrowing cost is 12.16%, so paying them 15 days early is worth that rate to them.
priceAsk.basis: Our current price sits at the top of the fair market band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg). They borrow money at 12.16%, so when we pay 15 days early we save them that cost — ask for it back as a price cut.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days instead of 30 days.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹26.60 L in cash for us, but it's worth that cost to them because their cash is stuck for 101 days (vs 64 for similar firms) — they need cash sooner.

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.3% as profit on every ₹100 they sell, so there's very little room for a pure price squeeze. But their cash is stuck for 101 days vs 64 days at similar firms, and they borrow at 12.16% — so paying them faster is genuinely valuable to them. They owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr of debt) and have delayed EPF payments, a sign cash is tight. We are 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue — small but not trivial. The win is trading faster payment for a price cut, not squeezing margin they don't have.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck far longer than competitors — 101 days vs 64 days.
They borrow money at about 12%, so paying early saves them that rate.
They keep only a tiny slice as profit — 2.3% of every ₹100 sold.
They carry significant debt — 1.25 times their own cash.
evidence.figure: Debt vs equity: 1.25x; total debt ₹282.62 Cr

evidence.point: We spend ₹6.47 Cr with them, which is 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue.
Their credit rating is middling (CARE BBB+ / Stable) and they've delayed EPF payments.
evidence.figure: Rating: CARE BBB+ / Stable; risk flag: EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volume — proven and scalable for laminate sachets (revenue ₹2755.75 Cr, health C 58/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale (revenue ₹16492.00 Cr, health C 46/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong fit for our sachets (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100).

risks: They sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.36) — not distressed but not robust. A hard price squeeze could tip supply; lead with the payment-for-discount swap instead.
EPF payment delays and high debt (1.25x equity) are red flags for cash tightness — line up Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a qualified second source before pushing hard.
Their profit is paper-thin (2.3%) — if we push price without giving them faster payment, they may not be able to deliver or may cut quality to stay afloat.
We are only 0.61% of their revenue — we have less weight to throw around than with a smaller supplier, so the ask must be commercially fair (the payment-speed trade is).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 15-day payment to help your cash flow — and in return we're looking for a price adjustment that reflects the financing cost we're saving you, around 12%.
